correctness.rationale: In GF(2)[(Z/2)^n], write translations t_i=1+y_i with y_i²=0. The exact third-shell expansion is A_n=binom(n,3)+binom(n−1,2)e1+(n−2)e2+e3, giving residue classes e1(1+e2), e2(1+e1), e1e2 and 1+e1+e2+e3. Frobenius proves (A_n+c_n)^2=0 with c_n=1 iff n≡3 mod4. For n≡0,3 mod4 the shifted element is a coordinate under a unit/triangular change, rank 2^(n−1); for n≡1 use alternating normal form of e2 in odd n and field Künneth to get 2^(n−1)-2^((n−1)/2); for n≡2 reduce e1e2 to z e2 in n−1 odd variables, rank 2^(n−2)-2^((n−2)/2). Jordan forms force all trajectory and cycle counts. Independently constructed distance-three matrices and exact GF2 row reduction agree at every n=3..10. Infinite assertion follows from the group-algebra proof.
residual_risks: Frobenius square-zero and field-Künneth computations apply only over GF2
